dashboard.title: From combustion data to safety decisions
dashboard.subtitle: IGNIS turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into clear evidence for designing fire-safety systems in spacecraft, stations, lunar bases, Mars bases, and pressurized rovers.
dashboard.coverageSubtitle: Distribution of the 24 PSI investigations and 6 NASA sources across prevention, detection, and suppression.
dashboard.featuredSubtitle: Investigations with the highest fire-safety relevance, selected with an explainable score.
dashboard.gapSubtitle: The gap map shows the intersections between safety needs and available evidence.
dashboard.scenarioSubtitle: Compute O₂ partial pressure, dimensionless numbers, and adiabatic flame temperature for a lunar base, rover, or the ISS.
dashboard.missionBody: IGNIS combines a language model, a fire-safety taxonomy, deterministic calculations, and evidence retrieval with citations. Every claim can be traced back to PSI or a publication.
dashboard.evidenceSummarizeBody: Clear explanations of objectives, methods, findings, and limitations.
dashboard.evidenceClassifyBody: Tags for phase, environment, fuel, gravity, sensors, and hardware.
dashboard.evidenceInterpretBody: Comparisons, evidence gaps, and scientific calculations for design decisions.
dashboard.earthBody: Microgravity research also informs water-mist extinguishers, smoke detection, and safer firefighter equipment.
dashboard.dataBody: The snapshot is built from the public NASA PSI API. Citations, DOIs, and experimental-table links remain visible.
dashboard.copilotTitle: Ask like an engineer. Receive traceable evidence.
dashboard.copilotBody: Ummia does not improvise: it retrieves PSI investigations, cites them, and separates facts from calculations. Switch between student and engineer mode to adjust depth.
dashboard.copilotQ: What evidence exists for fire suppression in microgravity?
dashboard.copilotA: Evidence is concentrated in solid and liquid materials. BASS-II and FLEX measure extinguishment in microgravity and show that the absence of buoyancy changes the suppression mechanism: the agent must reach the flame through diffusion and forced convection, not natural thermal transport.
dashboard.ctaTitle: Explore the evidence. Design with judgment.
dashboard.ctaBody: All 30 evidence records, their publications, and their limits are one click away. Start with the gap map or ask Ummia directly.
dashboard.labNote: Oxygen partial pressure remains close to Earth's (3.09 psi) at a lower total pressure. Material flammability must be validated for that atmosphere.
dashboard.nextGenTitle: Controls and equipment already changing fire safety
dashboard.nextGenSubtitle: Four fronts where PSI research feeds detectors, suppression, responder protection, and material selection, both in orbit and on Earth.
dashboard.nextGenDetectionBody: SAME and SAME-R measured the size, concentration, and evolution of smoke particles in microgravity, where no rising plume exists. Those data calibrate detectors that must warn before smoke is visible, the basis of the fire detector transferred to terrestrial applications.
dashboard.nextGenDetectionEarth: Early detection in homes, tunnels, warehouses, aircraft cabins, and data centers.
dashboard.nextGenSuppressionBody: BASS-II and FLEX measured extinction limits and the effectiveness of gaseous agents in microgravity. The ISS portable fine water mist extinguisher uses microscopic droplets to cool and displace oxygen with a fraction of the water of a conventional sprinkler.
dashboard.nextGenSuppressionEarth: Spaces with electrical equipment, archives, kitchens, and areas where conventional water causes damage.
dashboard.nextGenProtectionBody: Thermal protection materials and air systems derived from aerospace research reduce weight and improve firefighter visibility, heat resistance, and endurance. Protective attire and air tanks are direct transfers of that technology.
dashboard.nextGenProtectionEarth: Lighter, heat-resistant clothing and longer-lasting air tanks for firefighters and industrial brigades.
dashboard.nextGenMaterialsBody: SAFFIRE I–III burned real samples aboard uncrewed spacecraft to measure growth, spread, and flammability limits in low gravity. Its data refine material-selection criteria and spread models that are also used on Earth.
dashboard.nextGenMaterialsEarth: Test and modeling criteria for transport, building, wiring, and technical textile materials.
dashboard.nextGenWaterMistLink: Fine water mist extinguisher · NASA NTRS

gaps.title: Gap map
gaps.subtitle: Cross fire-safety needs with the evidence available in PSI. Empty cells are research opportunities, not an absence of risk.
gaps.gapsSubtitle: Intersections without direct evidence in the current snapshot.
gaps.insightBody: Evidence is concentrated in microgravity and spacecraft/station environments. There is no partial-gravity data in PSI, and the lunar base, Mars, and rovers appear as direct-evidence gaps. That is a central conclusion of the challenge, not a defect of the dashboard.
gaps.partialGravityNote: Partial gravity is shown as its own dimension because the challenge brief identifies it as a data gap.
gaps.opportunityBody: Each empty cell indicates an operational condition that is not directly represented in the PSI snapshot. It does not mean the risk is absent: it means the decision requires analogies, ground testing, or new evidence.
gaps.strongestNote: Cells with the highest number of associated investigations.

metrics.title: Four pillars for measuring IGNIS impact
metrics.subtitle: What each module measures and what result it lets you defend with evidence. No invented targets or unmeasured data: each pillar connects a real platform capability to a verifiable metric.
metrics.tableBody: The four IGNIS pillars, what each one measures, and the metric that makes it verifiable.
metrics.tableScrollHint: Scroll horizontally to see the result column.
metrics.row1Measures: Efficiency in cross-referencing the {count} NASA PSI and Spinoff sources.
metrics.row1Result: From hours of manual review to direct on-screen comparison.
metrics.row2Measures: Prevention hypotheses for habitat and experiment design.
metrics.row2Result: Estimated ΔP as a hypothesis based on evidence; effectiveness not demonstrated.
metrics.row3Measures: Existing investigations by environment, separated into prevention, detection, and suppression.
metrics.row3Result: Identification of available evidence and gaps by environment and function.
metrics.row4Measures: Technical rigor and trust for education and research.
metrics.row4Result: Answers and calculations traceable to curated sources, with visible formulas and assumptions.
metrics.pillarsTitle: What each module measures and how it translates into impact
metrics.pillarsBody: The four pillars cover the full path: consulting evidence without friction, turning it into mitigation decisions, flagging where research is missing, and supporting every answer with traceability and reproducibility. Each pillar is assessed with metrics observable in the demo, not with pilot targets.
metrics.pillar1Intro: The Comparator places the 24 NASA PSI investigations and the 6 additional sources side by side, without forcing users to download and cross-reference raw files.
metrics.pillar1Metric1Body: How much time a user saves by evaluating the 30 curated sources side by side instead of searching, downloading, and cross-referencing files manually on NASA's original portal.
metrics.pillar1Metric2Body: Navigation and controls are available in Spanish and English while the original scientific records remain intact. It measures how quickly a student or researcher can filter evidence without losing technical precision.
metrics.pillar2Intro: The Laboratory turns a scenario into an estimated probability and a mitigation hypothesis. It does not prove effectiveness: it proposes what should be validated next.
metrics.pillar2Metric1Body: Difference between the initial combustion probability in microgravity under given parameters and the resulting probability after applying the mitigation measures suggested by the platform.
metrics.pillar2Metric2Body: Only hypotheses of possible outcomes are formulated from the available investigations. There is no evidence that the proposed mitigation is functional or successful; any application requires experimental validation.
metrics.pillar3Intro: The Gap Map organizes existing investigations by environment and separates them into prevention, detection, and suppression, showing what evidence exists and what is missing.
metrics.pillar3Metric1Body: The map gathers existing investigations for each environment and separates them into three functions: prevention, detection, and suppression. This shows what evidence is available and for which environment.
metrics.pillar3Metric2Body: Prevents future projects from repeating documented tests and shows where research is still missing.
metrics.pillar4Intro: Ummia SI consults only the 30 curated sources, and calculations are separated from generative models. Trust is demonstrated through traceability.
metrics.pillar4Metric1Body: Every Ummia SI answer points back to curated sources, and every calculation shows its formulas, assumptions, and limits. The platform separates evidence retrieval from text generation and never invents experimental values.
metrics.pillar4Metric2Body: Any third party can audit and regenerate the same 30-record PostgreSQL database with fetch_psi.py and seed.py, following open-science standards.
metrics.baseBody: Data you can check in the demo and the repository, without depending on a pilot.
metrics.basePublicationsHint: With a DOI or institutional link when available
metrics.baseLanguagesHint: ES/EN navigation and controls; original records intact
metrics.baseReproducibleHint: fetch_psi.py and seed.py scripts; 30 PostgreSQL records
metrics.beneficiariesBody: The four pillars translate into value for different profiles.
metrics.beneficiary1Body: Justify material, detector, and agent selection with cited evidence, and surface gaps before a design review.
metrics.beneficiary2Body: Train responses conditioned on available resources and rehearse the protocol before it is needed.
metrics.beneficiary3Body: Use the platform in Spanish or English to compare and cite publications; syntheses and PSI records remain in their original language, with traceability for theses, classes, or reviews.
metrics.beneficiary4Body: Connect space research to fine water mist, smoke detection, protective clothing, air tanks, and test criteria.
metrics.beneficiary5Title: Evaluators and the Space Apps community
metrics.beneficiary5Body: Find an auditable method, citable sources, and scripts to replicate the database.
metrics.ctaTitle: Explore the four pillars in the demo
metrics.ctaBody: Open the Comparator, calculate a scenario, review the Gap Map, or ask Ummia. Each module shows the evidence behind its metric.

about.title: Methodology and scope
about.subtitle: How IGNIS turns NASA PSI data into interpretable evidence without hiding uncertainty.
about.missionBody: IGNIS is a bilingual support dashboard for research and education in fire safety for space exploration. It summarizes, classifies, and interprets low-gravity combustion research.
about.dataBody: The snapshot is built from the public NASA PSI API. It includes 24 Combustion Science investigations, 6 complementary NASA sources, metadata, and publications. Restricted raw data is not included.
about.methodBody: Classification combines a curated review of the 24 PSI investigations and 6 NASA sources with a keyword classifier for new records. The relevance score is explainable and shown with its components. The language layer is separated from scientific calculations.
about.scienceBody: O₂ partial pressure, dimensionless numbers, and adiabatic temperatures are computed with formulas and deterministic libraries. Cantera is used for thermochemical equilibrium of supported fuels. Assumptions are shown in the interface.
about.limitsBody: There is no partial-gravity data in PSI. Raw files may require authentication. The tool does not certify safety, replace standardized testing, or serve as the sole basis for an operational decision.
about.roadmapBody: MVP: investigation comparator. Second iteration: Ummia SI creator and Laboratory. Vision: bring IGNIS to universities and NASA teams as the standard tool for data consultation and mitigation hypothesis modeling, scientifically backed to guide future real tests.
about.sourceBody: Data: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), NASA Spinoff, and NASA Glenn Research Center. IGNIS is an independent NASA Space Apps Challenge project and is not officially affiliated with NASA.
about.teamBody: Five-person team: product and UX, frontend, backend and data, AI/ML, and science/QA. Names will be added in the public version.
about.pipelineSubtitle: Every answer passes through four auditable layers before reaching the interface.
about.step1Body: Bilingual BM25 over titles, summaries, objectives, and findings. Filters by phase, environment, fuel, and gravity.
about.step2Body: Fire-safety taxonomy applied through curated review and explainable rules.
about.step3Body: Comparisons, gap map, and deterministic calculations separated from language generation.
about.step4Body: ES/EN answer with sources, confidence, and limits. The LLM is optional; local mode works without an API key.
about.archAIBody: Retrieval + rules + optional LLM (Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama)
about.roleProductBody: Narrative, user flow, visual identity, and demo.
about.roleFrontendBody: Next.js, components, i18n, accessibility, and performance.
about.roleBackendBody: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, PSI ingestion, API, and traceability.
about.roleAIBody: Retrieval, prompts, evaluation, and free providers.
about.roleScienceBody: Taxonomy, calculations, validation, and scientific limits.
about.reproBody: The snapshot can be regenerated with backend/scripts/fetch_psi.py and loaded into PostgreSQL with seed.py. Calculations show formulas, assumptions, and libraries. Answers without an LLM are deterministic.
about.visionBody: Our next step is to bring IGNIS to universities and NASA teams to position it as the standard tool for data consultation and mitigation hypothesis modeling in their Laboratory, scientifically backed to guide future real tests.
